overview: Dassault Systèmes is a French multinational software company and global leader in Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and 3D design software, providing 'virtual twin' and simulation platforms under brands including CATIA, SOLIDWORKS, ENOVIA, SIMULIA, DELMIA, MEDIDATA and BIOVIA, unified on its 3DEXPERIENCE platform. The Group serves roughly 390,000+ customers across three strategic sectors -- Manufacturing Industries, Life Sciences & Healthcare, and Infrastructure & Cities -- with operations spanning 11 GEOs (Americas, Europe/EMEA, Asia) and about 25,000 employees in 188 sites worldwide. It is majority-controlled (economically ~40%, ~54% of voting rights) by Groupe Industriel Marcel Dassault, the holding company of the Dassault family, and was spun off from Dassault Aviation in 1981.

business_model.summary: Dassault Systèmes sells engineering, design, simulation and data-management software through perpetual/periodic licenses and increasingly through multi-year subscription and cloud (SaaS) contracts, plus support/maintenance and professional services. Recurring software revenue (subscription + support) represented about 83% of software revenue in H1 2026, making the model heavily annuity-like; the company introduced Annual Run Rate (ARR) as a new headline KPI in February 2026 to track the subscription/cloud transition (ARR grew 6% YoY in constant currency to EUR4.44bn in Q2 2026).

revenue_streams.name: Software - Licenses and other
revenue_streams.trend: stable/declining as mix shifts to subscription

product_line_mix.name: Industrial Innovation (CATIA, ENOVIA, SIMULIA, DELMIA, GEOVIA)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise and mid-market, from startups to the largest global manufacturers, life sciences companies, and public/infrastructure bodies; sold via direct sales force and an indirect channel of ~18,000 partners/resellers/system integrators
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas ~39% of software revenue, Europe ~38%, Asia ~23% (H1 2026); active in 155-159 countries

main_competitors: Emerging AI-native entrants (Anthropic-backed CAD tools, Prometheus 'artificial general engineer')
competitive_position.market_position: One of the three global leaders (with Siemens and PTC) in PLM/engineering software for large manufacturers; Siemens, PTC, Dassault, Autodesk, SAP and Aras collectively account for roughly 80%+ of the PLM market. Dassault positions itself as the premium, end-to-end platform leader, particularly strong in aerospace & defense, automotive, and (via Medidata/BIOVIA) life sciences/clinical trials -- a domain where traditional CAD peers have little presence.

moat_factors.description: PLM/CAD deployments are deeply embedded in customers' engineering workflows, often spanning decades (average >25-year relationships with its top 20 clients); migrating off CATIA/ENOVIA is costly and disruptive.
3DEXPERIENCE unifies 3D modeling, simulation, data management and collaboration across design-to-manufacturing-to-usage lifecycle, a harder-to-replicate end-to-end offering versus point solutions.
Decades of accumulated know-how in regulated, safety-critical industries (aerospace, defense, pharma) create credibility and certification barriers that are hard for new entrants to match.
Flagship, long-standing relationships with Boeing, Airbus, Ford, Volkswagen and major pharma companies reinforce reputation, though this also creates concentration in cyclical end markets.
~18,000 partners/system integrators and 400+ software development partners extend reach, but also create a degree of channel dependency.

weaknesses: Heavy exposure to cyclical, capital-intensive end markets (automotive, aerospace) that can delay or cancel large IT investments
Medidata/Life Sciences segment has underperformed, with clinical trial study starts declining, dragging the overall growth rate
Perceived vulnerability to AI-native disruption narratives (e.g., Anthropic, Prometheus) even though actual product displacement has not yet materialized
Complex, overlapping twelve-brand portfolio can create go-to-market and integration friction, especially post-acquisition
Governance concentration -- GIMD/Dassault family controls ~54% of voting rights, limiting minority shareholder influence

growth_drivers: 3D UNIV+RSES (7th-generation platform) and AI-native offerings -- Virtual Companions, Generative Experiences, Virtual Twins as a Service -- aimed at monetizing AI atop the installed base
Continued cloud and 3DEXPERIENCE adoption: 3DEXPERIENCE software revenue +10% and cloud software revenue +11% in H1 2026 (3DEXPERIENCE Cloud +46%)
Subscription/SaaS transition lifting recurring revenue mix and introducing ARR as a new disclosure metric

M&A to expand addressable market: Enalean/Tuleap (ALM, cyber-systems, March 2026), and the pending ~$1.8-2.0bn acquisition of ArisGlobal (AI-native life-sciences regulatory/compliance platform, announced July 2026) to reinforce BIOVIA/MEDIDATA
Partnerships with NVIDIA (accelerated computing / 'Industry World Models') and Mistral AI (foundation models) to embed Industrial AI across the platform
Large estimated addressable market of ~$130bn across Manufacturing ($75bn), Life Sciences & Healthcare ($25bn) and Infrastructure & Cities ($30bn), leaving substantial penetration runway
Geographic and industry diversification across 12 industries and 11 GEOs cushioning any single end-market downturn
Mid-term ambition (reaffirmed at the June 2025 Capital Markets Day) to double non-IFRS diluted EPS by 2029, with an update expected at the November 17, 2026 Capital Markets Day

business.description: Company's top-ranked risk: customers in automotive, aerospace, energy and natural-resources industries may postpone, cancel or fail to renew large software investments amid geopolitical and economic uncertainty.

Growing market concentration, new SaaS/AI-native entrants, and local/national competitors in some geographies could pressure pricing and share, particularly as AI-native CAD tools (e.g., Anthropic-backed, Prometheus) are perceived as potential disruptors.

business.risk: Customer deployment delays, errors and product defects
business.description: Complex enterprise software deployments can run over budget/time; defects in released software can trigger customer claims and reputational damage.

business.risk: Organizational/operational complexity from growth and M&A integration
business.description: Twelve-brand portfolio and continued acquisitions (Enalean, ArisGlobal) raise integration, cultural and amortization/impairment risk.
Significant reliance on ~18,000 distributors/resellers/system integrators; disruption to key partners or hardware/cloud infrastructure suppliers could impair delivery.
Intense competition for AI talent; company does not insure against loss of key personnel.
License revenue is historically back-loaded into Q4 and the last month of each quarter, making quarterly results volatile and sensitive to order timing.

financial.description: Significant USD and JPY exposure; FY2026 guidance explicitly assumes $1.17/EUR and JPY177.1/EUR, with currency effects causing meaningful swings in reported vs constant-currency growth (e.g., H1 2026 total revenue -1% reported vs +4% constant currency).

Issued a new EUR1.0bn, 5-year bond at 3.375% in June 2026 to fund growth/refinance RCF; borrowings rose to EUR3.38bn (from EUR2.60bn at YE2025), though the company still held a EUR2.28bn net cash position at H1 2026 and carries an 'A' stable S&P rating.
OECD GloBE rules now apply in France since FY2024; company states no material impact so far but continues to monitor.

regulatory.description: Exposure to data protection/privacy (including health data), AI governance frameworks, export controls/sanctions (High-Tech products), anti-corruption and tax regulation across many countries.
Risk of claims that its products infringe third-party IP (including AI-related claims), and risk that its own IP protections are insufficient in some jurisdictions; also exposure to software piracy.

regulatory.risk: ArisGlobal and other pending M&A regulatory approval
regulatory.description: The ~$1.8-2.0bn ArisGlobal acquisition (announced July 2026) is subject to customary regulatory approvals and closing conditions before closing in H2 2026.

macro.description: Automotive (part of Transportation & Mobility) has been a drag; European software revenue growth has been impacted by weaker automotive demand.

Medidata exposed to the pace of clinical trial starts; Life Sciences software revenue declined 9% YoY in H1 2026 (3% in constant currency), and FY2025 guidance had already been cut in October 2025 partly due to Medidata softness.

Broad software-sector selloffs tied to fears that generative/agentic AI could compress the value of licensed enterprise software, which hit DSY.PA shares specifically in connection with Anthropic- and Prometheus-related CAD disruption narratives.
Falling interest rates reduced financial income on cash balances (H1 2026 net financial income down 23% YoY), a modest earnings headwind even as it benefits borrowing costs on new debt.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: PLM/3D design and simulation software market is a multi-vendor oligopoly (Siemens, PTC, Dassault, Autodesk, SAP, Aras collectively ~80%+ share) estimated to grow mid-single-digits to high-single-digits annually, with cloud/SaaS and AI-native features as the key battlegrounds. Dassault frames its addressable market at ~$130bn, well above its current ~$6.2bn revenue base, implying long runway if execution holds.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high indirect cyclicality via large capex-intensive customer industries (automotive, aerospace, energy); recurring software revenue (~83% of software revenue) dampens volatility versus a pure-license model, but new license/subscription growth and professional services remain sensitive to customer investment cycles.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct sensitivity (net cash position historically generated meaningful financial income that is now declining as rates fall); increasing modestly as the company has taken on more debt (EUR1bn bond issued June 2026) to fund M&A.
key_input_costs: Skilled R&D/engineering personnel costs (R&D ~20% of revenue)
Acquisition-related amortization of intangibles (~EUR315m guided for FY2026, mostly Medidata-related)

recent_developments.event: Stock remains well below its pre-February-2026 levels following the sharpest single-day decline in over two decades; market continues to digest AI-disruption narrative and weak Life Sciences trends ahead of the November Capital Markets Day.

Announced definitive agreement to acquire ArisGlobal, an AI-native enterprise compliance/regulatory platform for Life Sciences, for roughly $1.8bn (up to ~$2bn with AI-linked earnouts), to close H2 2026, strengthening BIOVIA/MEDIDATA; also reported H1 2026 results (non-IFRS operating margin flat at 30.1%, Life Sciences software revenue -9% reported/-3% constant currency).

Issued EUR1.0bn, 5-year senior unsecured bond at 3.375% coupon (significantly oversubscribed) and refinanced its revolving credit facility, funding M&A and shareholder returns while maintaining an 'A' stable S&P rating.
Finalized acquisition of Enalean (Tuleap ALM platform), integrated with CATIA to strengthen Model-Based Systems Engineering and cyber-systems strategy for regulated industries.

Co-founder and Chairman Bernard Charlès abruptly stepped down for personal reasons; CEO Pascal Daloz became Chairman and CEO. Charlès remains engaged in an advisory capacity on the 3D UNIV+RSES/AI vision.

Shares fell roughly 19-21% intraday/close -- the steepest drop in over two decades -- after Q4 2025 revenue (EUR1.68bn, -4.1% YoY) missed consensus (~EUR1.74bn) and FY2026 guidance (revenue EUR6.29-6.41bn, EPS EUR1.30-1.34) came in well below market expectations (~EUR6.58bn revenue, ~EUR1.37 EPS); weakness attributed to automotive/pharma demand softness, Medidata clinical-trial declines, and a broader sector selloff driven by fears of AI-native disruption (Anthropic, Prometheus 'artificial general engineer' CAD tools).
Cut FY2025 revenue growth guidance to 4-6% from a prior 6-8% range, citing fresh weakness at Medidata tied to declining starts of life-science studies.

At its Capital Markets Day, reaffirmed/pushed back its mid-term ambition to double non-IFRS diluted EPS, now targeting 2029 (vs. the prior 2023-2028 framework); introduced the 3D UNIV+RSES 7th-generation platform vision; BofA called the EPS doubling target 'ambitious' versus consensus.

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Half-Year Report / Q2 2026 results (confirmed following Q2 2026 results)

items.notes: Implies 1-3% reported growth; 3-5% growth at constant exchange rates. This is the same range set at Q4 2025 results in February 2026 (which itself represented a steep cut versus prior expectations of ~EUR6.58bn).
Full-year objective; H1 2026 non-IFRS operating margin was already 30.1%, flat YoY.
Implies roughly -1% to +2% growth at current exchange rates, or +3% to +6% at constant exchange rates vs FY2025's EUR1.31.
Principal currency assumptions underlying the non-IFRS objectives; guidance excludes new acquisitions/restructuring completed after June 30, 2026 (i.e., excludes ArisGlobal impact until closing).
Estimate excludes any new grants issued after June 30, 2026.
Largely driven by the Medidata acquisition; excluded from non-IFRS objectives.

items.target: EUR4.44 billion (Q2 2026 actual, +6% YoY constant currency)
items.notes: New metric introduced to track subscription/cloud transition; no explicit full-year ARR target disclosed yet.

items.metric: Mid-term ambition: double non-IFRS diluted EPS
items.vs_prior: pushed back one year at June 2025 Capital Markets Day
items.notes: An update on this ambition, and on AI monetization, is expected at the next Capital Markets Day on November 17, 2026.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO and Chairman Pascal Daloz has framed 2026 as the year to convert the 3D UNIV+RSES platform and AI-native offerings (Virtual Companions, Generative Experiences, Virtual Twins as a Service) into tangible value, emphasizing resilience in the core business (software revenue, 3DEXPERIENCE +10% and cloud +8-11% in 2025/H1 2026) despite macro uncertainty, automotive/Life-Sciences softness, and investor fears that AI-native tools could disrupt traditional engineering software. Management reiterated it will provide further detail on AI strategy and its mid-term financial ambition at the November 17, 2026 Capital Markets Day.

bull_case: High-quality, sticky recurring revenue base (~83% of software revenue is subscription/support) embedded in mission-critical engineering workflows across aerospace, automotive and life sciences, with switching costs that are very high

Large underpenetrated addressable market (~$130bn) versus ~EUR6.2bn current revenue, with 3DEXPERIENCE, cloud and new AI-native offerings (Virtual Companions, Generative Experiences, Virtual Twins as a Service) as fresh monetization vectors
Strong balance sheet (net cash position, 'A' stable S&P rating) funding continued bolt-on and platform-expanding M&A (ArisGlobal, Enalean) without straining the capital structure

February 2026 selloff (-20%+) may have overshot fundamentals if AI proves additive (via NVIDIA/Mistral partnerships) rather than disruptive to Dassault's science-based, regulated-industry-focused platform, creating a potential re-rating catalyst at the November 2026 Capital Markets Day

Durable competitive moat in a concentrated three-to-six-player PLM oligopoly (Siemens, PTC, Dassault, Autodesk, SAP, Aras) with decades-long customer relationships averaging 25+ years with top accounts
bear_case: Two consecutive guidance cuts (Oct 2025 and Feb 2026) and a steep, confidence-denting stock crash suggest deteriorating visibility into forward growth, particularly from Medidata/Life Sciences and automotive end-markets

Credible, still-unresolved narrative that AI-native/agentic CAD tools (Anthropic-backed efforts, Prometheus) could disintermediate traditional licensed engineering software over the medium term, pressuring the multiple even without near-term revenue impact

Abrupt, unexplained exit of long-time Chairman/co-founder Bernard Charlès in February 2026 (described by one outlet as following a sharp share-price drop) raises governance and succession-stability questions, even with Daloz's continuity as CEO/Chairman
Heavy dependence on cyclical capital-goods end markets (automotive, aerospace) and clinical-trial volumes (Medidata) for growth, with limited near-term visibility into when these segments recover

Mid-term 'double EPS by 2029' ambition was already pushed back once (from the original 2023-2028 framework) and was called 'ambitious' by at least one major sell-side analyst, raising the risk of a further reset at the November 2026 Capital Markets Day
Family/GIMD control (~54% of voting rights) limits the influence of minority shareholders over strategic and capital-allocation decisions, including M&A such as the ~$1.8-2.0bn ArisGlobal deal
